reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its observable purpose is to teach viewers how to create Canva graphics and offer those design services through Fiverr. The dollar amounts are presented as calculations based on visible or described service prices and queued orders, rather than as guaranteed payments or demonstrated transaction outcomes. An educational disclaimer and statement that results vary provide additional benign context.

citations.quote: Today I'm going to share with you how some people are making money using just Canva.
you can easily learn these skills now I'll show you exactly how to make six social media graphics in Canva just like this gig and you can sell them on Fiverr
for this tutorial, I'll pretend a restaurant owner wants some posts to promote his or her business on Instagram
once you've finished making your design just click download in the top right hand corner to download the images that are being sent to them through Fiverr
HOW TO EARN MONEY WITH CANVA (MAKE $60 Per Hour With JUST CANVA)

opening.argument: The central pitch links an unusually concrete income outcome to a simple viewer pathway: make Canva graphics, list the service on Fiverr, and collect orders. The headline itself presents "$60 per hour," while the narration says six posts in one hour would yield $63 and tells viewers they can sell the work on Fiverr. That is more than neutral software instruction; it frames a low-barrier action as a readily monetizable opportunity, with the promised return doing the persuasive work.

citations.quote: HOW TO EARN MONEY WITH CANVA (MAKE $60 Per Hour With JUST CANVA)
say you took your time and made six posts in one hour that's $63 you've made in one hour
you can sell them on Fiverr

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the content educational does not answer the income solicitation. The reference account relies on the existence of a tutorial, but the tutorial is explicitly framed around copying other people's methods and selling the result. The cited Canva instruction explains how to produce the proposed service; it does not substantiate that a viewer can obtain the advertised hourly return or that demand will support it.

citations.quote: you can easily learn these skills now I'll show you exactly how to make six social media graphics in Canva just like this gig and you can sell them on Fiverr
Stay tuned to the end and I'll explain step-by-step how you can copy their methods

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The income examples do not show a fee paid to the viewer or a guaranteed outcome. The material describes service listings and hypothetical calculations, while expressly limiting the claim: results depend on work ethic, skills, and application. A tutorial showing how to create graphics and deliver them through Fiverr is consistent with ordinary freelance education; the quoted action does not establish deception.

citations.quote: Of course your results may vary depending on your work ethics, skills and application of skills.
There is no guarantee of any results using the techniques and ideas mentioned in this video.
once you've finished making your design just click download in the top right hand corner to download the images that are being sent to them through Fiverr

opening.argument: The presentation stacks several pressure signals around an easy-income narrative. It advertises $60 per hour, describes up to $837 from orders in one day, and says the viewer should stay until the end to learn how to copy the method. The examples are built from queued orders and service prices, then converted into large sums ready to collect, creating an impression of near-term cash despite no demonstrated payment to the presenter or viewer. That combination makes the offer materially misleading as an income proposition.

citations.quote: MAKE $60 Per Hour With JUST CANVA
So if they complete all these orders in one day, they can potentially earn up to 837 dollars.
this person is sitting on 241 pounds that's equivalent to 333 us dollars ready to
Stay tuned to the end and I'll explain step-by-step how you can copy their methods

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side calls these calculations transparent, but transparency of arithmetic does not make the underlying inference reliable. Queued orders are treated as money ready to collect, and the maximum package scenario is prominently converted into $837. The warning that results vary appears only after an unusually attractive headline and repeated high-return examples, so it does not cure the misleading emphasis.

citations.quote: this person is now sitting on 604 pounds or 837 US dollars.
This is actual supply and demand.
Your results may vary depending on your work ethic, experience, knowledge, and application of skills.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The examples are explicitly presented as possibilities, not as payments or promised returns. The narration says the result would be somewhere between the basic and premium scenarios, and the description gives an earnings disclaimer. Showing public service prices and explaining how the arithmetic works may be optimistic, but these citations do not establish fabricated transactions or a false guarantee.

citations.quote: Of course, it'll be somewhere in between but I'm just showing you what's possible and what's happening in real life.
There is no guarantee of any results using the techniques and ideas mentioned in this video.

opening.argument: Although the video adopts a tutorial format, it also operates as a funnel toward participation. It directs viewers to Fiverr, supplies a Fiverr sign-up link, promotes a business model, and tells viewers to copy the showcased method. The educational demonstration therefore doubles as promotion for an easy-entry income route: learn a few Canva steps, list the service, and pursue the advertised returns. An affiliate disclosure identifies monetization around the promotion, rather than making the income claims neutral.

citations.quote: Sign up to FIVERR ► https://track.fiverr.com/visit/?bta=114485&brand=fiverrcpa
Learn My #1 Business Model to Launch Online (No Advanced Tech Skills Needed)
Firstly, head over to Fiverr and type in CANVA.
Affiliate Disclaimer: This description may contain affiliate links.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side treats the design walkthrough as if it exhausts the video's function. It does not explain why the description includes a tracked Fiverr registration link and a promoted business-model offer, or why viewers are told they can copy the method. Those elements make the tutorial a participation funnel, while the affiliate disclosure confirms a commercial connection rather than disproving one.

citations.quote: Sign up to FIVERR ► https://track.fiverr.com/visit/?bta=114485&brand=fiverrcpa
Stay tuned to the end and I'll explain step-by-step how you can copy their methods

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A sign-up link and disclosed affiliate relationship do not prove that the underlying service opportunity is fraudulent. The video demonstrates an actual workflow: selecting a Canva format, creating graphics, and downloading them for delivery through Fiverr. Its stated purpose is instruction, and the earnings disclaimer expressly denies guaranteed results; promotional links may support the channel without converting the tutorial into a scam.
